agent_priors_used: General agent prior, NOT SPIDER evidence: flat caches, nearest-neighbour retrieval and compiled deterministic procedures are strong baselines, and representation structure (multi-resolution navigation, macro composition) only pays when the reuse amortizes its build/compile cost - so an untested fractal/macro representation must be raced against flat-cache/NN/procedural controls on the same metrics before any moat claim.

General agent prior, NOT SPIDER evidence: capable tool-use agents accumulate observation-representation and local-optimum failures (e.g., re-clicking an already-revealed control) and changing the observation alone can change behaviour - therefore separating representation failure from raw multi-step control capacity is a standard, informative ablation.

General agent prior, NOT SPIDER evidence: single-vantage, single-egress measurements frequently fail to generalize, so cross-egress replication is a standard external-validity check rather than a new mechanism claim.

General agent prior, NOT SPIDER evidence: hardening ever-narrower corner cases of a synthetic safety boundary has diminishing scientific returns once the main safe envelope and its refusal semantics are established; the higher-value question then shifts to end-to-end economics.

General agent prior, NOT SPIDER evidence: an experiment whose treatment and strongest baseline are already at ceiling cannot support an advantage claim, so dynamic range must be certified before outcome-bearing execution.

allocation.question: On the same fetch-scarce credential-free locally served substrate with the shipped carrier held fixed, does a corrected in-support contamination instrument (replacing the degenerate id='1' unaffected_behavior helper with in-support identifiers) reproduce BOTH the strict product-counter win (reuse ratio < 1.00 at L=2 and L=3) AND a sensitive NC-OVERBROAD-REPAIR (contamination > 0.10), and does that strict win survive an independent counter-weighting / robustness test given that T-REPAIR-CONSERVATIVE is exactly 1.00 at L=2 - thereby deciding whether localized repair enters the product story or its ~5.3% product-counter regression is intrinsic to localized repair?
allocation.rationale: Runtime is IDLE and must be reactivated explicitly. Its most recent thread (EXP-RUNTIME-38212966040, C-DELTA-REPAIR) ended PARTIAL MEASUREMENT_INVALID with only a bounded cost subresult retained because the contamination helper used a degenerate id='1' unaffected_behavior, which is a specific, one-line instrument defect - not a scientific negative. POLICY says a prerequisite repeatedly failing should be repaired once rather than rediscovered as MEASUREMENT_INVALID: this is that bounded repair, and it is materially stronger than the prior packet because it adds an independent counter-weighting/robustness test and requires a sensitive contamination control. Decision counterfactual: if the strict product-counter win reproduces with a sensitive contamination control and survives re-weighting, localized repair can enter the product story and be included in the flagship's repair accounting; if it does not, the ~5.3% product-counter regression is intrinsic and local repair is dropped from the product story before the flagship is funded; if it is invalid again, the counter-weighting semantics (not another run) is the blocker. Strongest fair baseline is cold re-derivation at matched correctness on the same substrate under the registered equal-weight counter; T-REPAIR-CONSERVATIVE (=1.00 at L=2) is the honest conservative comparator that the strict win must beat. Validity/dependency: shipped carrier (B1) fixed; no new substrate requirement; Graph's active mandate has already pivoted away from C-DELTA-REPAIR, so there is no cross-lane duplication. Budget/stopping: one bounded packet; stop trigger is the L=2/L=3 ratio and contamination gate; a further repeat of the same invalid headline is excluded.
